{{Quote|I can dance. If I could have one wish&hellip;''"<br />"''What?''"<br />''"I would dance the perfect dance. Once. It wouldn't matter who watched. I would know it was perfect.|Oola and Yarna d'al' Gargan|<ref name="Oola's Tale">{{StoryCite|story=A Time to Mourn, a Time to Dance: Oola's Tale|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}}</ref>}}
'''Oola''' was a [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] dancer in [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt's]] court. She was the daughter of a clan chieftain on [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]] and tricked into becoming a dancer by [[Bib Fortuna/Legends|Bib Fortuna]] and [[Jerris Rudd]] as a gift to Jabba. She was also the half-sister of [[Nolaa Tarkona]], the leader of the [[Diversity Alliance]]. She was eaten alive by the [[Jabba's rancor/Legends|rancor in Jabba's palace]], but by then she had already decided that death was far better than another day as Jabba's slave.

==Biography==
===Before Jabba's Palace===
{{Quote|Won't you let me help you? You won't get a second&hellip; chance. Do you know 'chance'?''"<br />"''We've been chosen to dance in Jabba's palace, the grandest on Tatooine. We're a pair. We go to Jabba together.''"<br />"''It's the grandest on Tatooine, all right. But I have business there. It won't be pleasant. Jabba's palace isn't what you think.|Luke Skywalker offers Oola a chance|<ref name="Oola's Tale" />}}
[[File:BibFortuna-SWE.png|thumb|275x275px|Oola was abducted by Bib Fortuna.|left]]
Oola was a [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Gender/Legends|female]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]].<ref name="CharEnc" /> By [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="The Essential Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' sets [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']] at the start of [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], and in "[[A Time to Mourn, a Time to Dance: Oola's Tale]]," Oola last saw her father four months prior; therefore, he achieved his position during or prior to [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].</ref> [[Oola's father/Legends|Oola's father]] was the renowned chief of his [[Ryloth Clan|eight hundred–person clan]],<ref name="Oola's Tale" /> granting both himself and his family considerable power and influence. Despite this, he provided Oola with little or no formal education, as Twi'lek society held that educating women was a threat to male authority. She instead devoted herself to dancing, which won her dozens of admirers, including the visiting Twi'lek criminal [[Bib Fortuna/Legends|Bib Fortuna]].<ref name="FF" /> Clan custom gave Oola's [[Parent/Legends|father]] the right to sell her, but Fortuna had doubts that the chief would agree to this. Instead of paying her father, he abducted and [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] Oola.<ref name="Oola's Tale" />

To increase their value, Fortuna purchased expensive dance education for Oola and another Twi'lek he had captured, [[Sienn'rha]]. They received four [[Standard month/Legends|months]] of training with the court dancers on Ryloth. Though Oola could not escape her enslavement, she loved to dance and saw her clan's traditions as a preservation of dignity and faith that the court dancers lacked. Oola was protective of Sienn, who was younger and more vulnerable. The first [[Human/Legends|Human]] that Oola ever met, [[Jerris Rudd]], assisted Fortuna with transporting the enslaved dancers to [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] for delivery to [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]]. They were initially delayed by [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] inspecting their vehicle, searching for the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="Oola's Tale" />

When Rudd told the Twi'leks to hide from predators until he returned, Oola and Sienn were fearful. Skywalker, who was indeed on Tatooine, sensed their fear and located them. He recognized their enslavement and tried to convince both Twi'leks to leave with him. Fortuna and his people had lied to Oola about the conditions that awaited her; they had claimed that her new master would be handsome, that she would be surrounded by luxury at the Palace while her audience appreciated her dancing, and that the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] was worse than the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]]. Oola thus doubted Skywalker's claim that he could bring her to safety with the Rebel Alliance, and wanted to see what Palace life was like, naively thinking she would be able to leave at any time. However, she knew Sienn was vulnerable, and helped the girl escape with Skywalker by holding Fortuna back while Skywalker used his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] to defeat Rudd. Oola allowed Fortuna to believe that she had merely wanted no rivals at Jabba's Palace, and he delivered her to [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]].<ref name="Oola's Tale" />

===At Jabba's Palace===
{{Quote|That's the difference between us. For all of your six million forms of communication, you're faithless.''"<br />"''I beg your pardon. I have every faith in Master Luke. He will rescue me.''"<br />"''Perhaps I can survive this. I'll do my b&mdash;|Oola and C-3PO, before being interrupted by Jabba the Hutt|<ref name="Oola's Tale" />}}
Oola quickly learned that she had been lied to about everything. She was immediately punished for helping Sienn escape after a fortune was spent on each girl. Rather than the customary dancing veils she had envisioned, she was forced to wear only a flimsy net costume loosely held together by narrow leather strips, and a headpiece that nearly deafened her. Jabba was immediately enamored with her and kept her chained by the neck to his throne as his personal property. Over the course of two [[Standard day/Legends|days]] and nights, she could not sleep and was forced to dance for the [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]]. She was only thrown scraps of food if she groveled to Jabba, along with food that the Hutt suspected was poisoned. She tested each of her chain's links, hoping to break them and escape, but found that none were weak enough. The few words of [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]] she knew meant "no," "please no," and "emphatically no," which she used to reject the Hutt's advances. As punishment, his [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] guards beat her, but in a way that did not leave her with any disfiguring bruises; she wished they had so that she might become repulsive to the Hutt. She was determined to escape from her horrible existence, whether by getting free from the palace or by death. Unlike her fellow dancer, the [[Askajian/Legends|Askajian]] [[Yarna d'al' Gargan/Legends|Yarna d'al' Gargan]], she did not believe it was worth enduring anything just to survive, as the Great Dance and bright, clean eternity awaited beyond [[Death/Legends|Death]].<ref name="Oola's Tale" />

[[File:JabbasDais-BtM.jpg|thumb|224x224px|Oola sat on Jabba's dais.]]
When she witnessed Jabba execute a prisoner by feeding him to [[Jabba's rancor/Legends|his rancor]], she was terrified so much that she forced herself onto Jabba and climbed over him so she wouldn’t have to watch anymore. Not long after,<ref name="Oola's Tale" /> the [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] arrived with a message for Jabba the Hutt from Skywalker,<ref name="RotJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> whom she recognized from their encounter mere days before. Oola was able to speak with C-3PO, who told her that Skywalker was indeed going to return to rescue them. Just as she expressed a renewed hope that she would have a second chance to escape with Skywalker, Jabba pulled her chain and half-strangled her to enjoy the feeling of having her body upon his own and the tickles of her trying to get off.<ref name="Oola's Tale" />

===Death and legacy===
{{Quote|Na chuba negatorie! Na! Na! Natoota&hellip;|Oola's final words|<ref name="Oola's Tale" />}}
[[File:OolaRancorPit-ROTJ.png|thumb|250px|Oola lands in the pit of the rancor|left]]
During the [[Max Rebo Band/Legends|Max Rebo Band's]] performance of "[[Jedi Rocks/Legends|Jedi Rocks]],"<ref name="RotJ" /> Oola danced for the last time. She felt a sense of rapture at finally perfecting her style of dancing and was determined to continue defying Jabba. Initially more angry than frightened,<ref name="Oola's Tale" /> Oola refused when he pulled on her chain and grabbed her end to haul it back. He became furious and tugged harder, bringing her over the trapdoor in front of his throne.<ref name="RotJ" /> She was terrified but used her few words of Huttese to continue telling him no.<ref name="Oola's Tale" /> Struggling to resist,<ref name="FF">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 96|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 96]]</ref> Oola was pulled closer to Jabba.<ref name="RotJ" />

His patience frayed,<ref name="FF96" /> the Hutt pressed a button on his throne, opening up a section of the floor beneath Oola.<ref name="Sleight of Hand: The Tale of Mara Jade">{{StoryCite|story=Sleight of Hand: The Tale of Mara Jade|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}}</ref> Jabba had dropped her into the rancor pit to suffer the same fate as others who resisted him, and she was eaten alive by the rancor.<ref name="LUP">{{StoryCite|story=Let Us Prey: The Whiphid's Tale|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}}</ref> Her legend, however, would live on in the form of impersonator [[Dame Needa]], who put on a nightly Oola tribute show at the [[Gardulla Oola]] hotel and casino in Mos Eisley.<ref name="RotJ" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|There's one dance she won't do no matter how much he pays her.|Mara Jade, on Oola|<ref name="Radio drama">[[Return of the Jedi (radio)|'' Return of the Jedi'' radio drama]]</ref>}}
[[File:Oola_defies_Jabba.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Oola defies Jabba.]]
Oola, like many female Twi'leks, was vain and naive, though those traits gave her optimism.<ref name="FF96">{{FactFile|96|TWI 19-22|Twi'leks}}</ref> Oola started envisioning what Jabba and his palace were like before she even met him. Only using what Bib Fortuna told her, she envisioned that Jabba would be handsome, suave, and impressed with her.<ref name="Oola's Tale" />

Oola was repulsed by her new master, and yet afraid for her own life if she refused his demands. This led her to try to dance far away from Jabba. Apparently, she was scared of the rancor more than she was of Jabba. However, her thoughts and emotions would make her careless. When she heard that Skywalker was coming, she performed her best dance. She hoped that he would be pleased by it when he arrived to free her.<ref name="Oola's Tale" />

Oola was naive, foolish, innocent, headstrong, self-delusional,<ref name="FF96" /> proud,<ref name="Oola's Tale" /> vain, and optimistic. At Jabba's Palace, she was forced to develop a callous persona.<ref name="FF96" /> Before Oola arrived in Jabba's palace her pride and jealousy flared up when Luke Skywalker was trying to rescue her.<ref name="Oola's Tale" /> She selfishly believed that she would become wealthy if she continued to work at Jabba's palace.<ref name="Reader's Companion">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> Instead of winning Jabba's favor all to herself as she had planned, the mistreatment of her as a slave was a result of costing Jabba his second slave girl.<ref name="Oola's Tale" />

==Equipment==
During her time at the palace, Oola wore a flimsy net costume secured by leather straps,<ref name="CharEnc" /> sandals, and a headpiece she can barely hear through.<ref name="Oola's Tale" /> A metal collar was locked around her neck, attached to a long rope-like chain with a tassel on the other end.<ref name="RotJ" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I remember doing ''Jedi'' in the daytime, then taking off my green make-up and going across town to put my cat make-up on in the evening.|Femi Taylor, who filmed her role as Oola while performing in ''Cats''|<ref name="Insider 34">{{InsiderCite|34|In the Star Wars Universe|In the ''Star Wars'' Universe: Femi Taylor}}</ref>}}
Oola was portrayed by actress and dancer [[Femi Taylor]] in the [[1983]] [[original trilogy]] film, {{Film|VI}}. Taylor portrayed Oola in both the original release and in additional scenes filmed later for the [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]]. The producer of the Special Edition, [[Rick McCallum]], had also produced an episode of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Young_Indiana_Jones_Chronicles ''The Young Indiana Jones Chronicles''], which Taylor's brother, [[Benedict Taylor]], starred in. After learning of the Special Edition, Taylor told McCallum that his sister was in the same shape as she was during the original shoot.<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|oola|Oola}}</ref> Since she had not significantly changed in appearance during the intervening 14 years, she wore her original costume with a new headpiece and was filmed in close-ups, showing terror as the rancor approached.<ref name="Insider 34" />

Oola's design was used for the generic Twi'lek dancer enemies in ''[[Super Star Wars: Return of the Jedi]]''.<ref name="SSW">''[[Super Star Wars: Return of the Jedi]]''</ref>
